questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. The base is clean and indurated. Dark-field microscopy reveals spiral organisms. Which of the following is the drug of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose — the gold standard. Dark-field microscopy showing spirochetes confirms the diagnosis. Doxycycline is an alternative for penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman from Bihar presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on trunk and thickened great auricular nerve. Slit-skin smear is negative. What is the leprosy classification according to Ridley-Jopling?
questions.exp: Borderline tuberculoid (BT) leprosy presents with multiple (2-5) hypopigmented anaesthetic patches, thickened peripheral nerves, and negative or scanty bacilli on slit-skin smear (PB or paucibacillary). TT has a single lesion; BL and LL have numerous lesions with positive smears.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic man presents with a rapidly expanding black eschar on the face extending to the palate. CT scan shows invasion of the paranasal sinuses. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis is caused by Rhizopus arrhizus (formerly R. oryzae) most commonly, especially in diabetic ketoacidosis. It presents with rapidly spreading black eschar, palatal necrosis, and sinus involvement. Treatment is liposomal amphotericin B plus surgical debridement.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with grouped tense vesicles on an erythematous base over the elbow and knees. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) shows granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) shows granular IgA deposits at dermal papillae tips on DIF — pathognomonic finding. It is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Linear IgA disease shows linear IgA at BMZ. BP shows IgG/C3 at BMZ.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasia on the nose for 2 years. Histology shows palisading nuclei at the periphery of tumour islands with retraction artifact. The most appropriate first-line treatment is:
opts: Wide local excision with 1 cm margins
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) on the nose — a high-risk H-zone location — is best treated with Mohs micrographic surgery, which offers the highest cure rate (~99%) with maximum tissue conservation. Wide excision with 1 cm margins is used for high-risk BCC elsewhere but Mohs is preferred on the face.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman with SLE develops a photosensitive facial rash. She is on hydroxychloroquine. Her anti-Ro/SSA antibodies are strongly positive. What skin finding is most characteristic of subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE)?
opts: Papulosquamous or annular polycyclic lesions on sun-exposed areas
questions.exp: SCLE presents with papulosquamous (psoriasiform) or annular/polycyclic lesions on photosensitive distribution (upper chest, back, arms). It is strongly associated with anti-Ro/SSA antibodies. Discoid lesions with scarring are characteristic of chronic CLE (DLE), not SCLE.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with Nikolsky sign positive, flaccid bullae, and oral erosions. DIF shows net-like intercellular IgG deposits in epidermis. The antigen targeted is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets Desmoglein 3 (Dsg3) — a desmosomal cadherin. Mucosal-dominant PV targets Dsg3 alone; mucocutaneous PV targets both Dsg3 and Dsg1. DIF shows intercellular IgG 'fish-net/chicken-wire' pattern. BP180 is target in bullous pemphigoid; collagen VII in EBA.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with fever, lymphadenopathy, and a polymorphic rash including macules, papules, and target lesions after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal necrosis. BSA detachment is 40%. This is classified as:
questions.exp: TEN (Lyell syndrome) involves >30% BSA detachment. SJS has <10% BSA; SJS-TEN overlap is 10-30%. Causative drugs include sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol, and NSAIDs. SSSS is caused by staphylococcal exfoliative toxin and affects children, with subcorneal split.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl presents with streaky hyperpigmentation following lines of Blaschko on the trunk since childhood. Biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with melanin incontinence. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Incontinentia pigmenti (IP) stage III (pigmentary stage) shows whorled/streaky hyperpigmentation along Blaschko lines due to melanin incontinence. Histology shows melanophages in dermis with basal vacuolar change. It is X-linked dominant (IKBKG gene), affecting females predominantly.

questions.q: A 40-year-old farmer presents with a nodule on the dorsum of hand that developed after a thorn prick 3 months ago. It then spread proximally in a linear pattern along the lymphatics to the axilla. Culture grows thermal dimorphic fungus. The drug of choice is:
questions.exp: Sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii) classically presents as lymphocutaneous nodules. It is a thermal dimorphic fungus. SSKI (potassium iodide) is the traditional first-line treatment, especially in resource-limited settings. Itraconazole 100-200 mg/day is the preferred systemic alternative. Amphotericin B is for severe/disseminated disease.

questions.q: A neonate presents with diffuse erythema and superficial bullae that rupture easily leaving a moist base. The Nikolsky sign is positive. Blood cultures grow coagulase-positive staphylococci. The split in the skin occurs at:
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B from S. aureus phage group II, which cleave Desmoglein 1 in the granular layer (stratum granulosum), producing a subcorneal split. This is different from TEN where the split is at the DEJ with full-thickness epidermal necrosis.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with erythematous scaly plaques on scalp, elbows, and knees for 10 years with nail pitting and onycholysis. He now has swollen interphalangeal joints. CASPAR criteria confirm psoriatic arthritis. Which biologic is approved for both skin and joint disease?
questions.exp: Secukinumab (anti-IL-17A) is approved for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis AND psoriatic arthritis. Ixekizumab (also anti-IL-17A) and ustekinumab (anti-IL-12/23) are similarly dual-approved. Dupilumab is for atopic dermatitis; omalizumab for chronic urticaria; mepolizumab for eosinophilic conditions.

questions.q: A 70-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal-appearing skin of trunk and thighs. DIF shows linear C3 and IgG at the BMZ. ELISA detects antibodies against the NC16A domain. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid targets BP180 (collagen XVII, NC16A domain) and BP230. It presents with tense bullae on urticarial base in the elderly. DIF shows linear IgG and/or C3 at the BMZ (n-serrated). Anti-BP180 ELISA is sensitive and specific. MMP targets integrin α6β4 and laminins.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4 = 120) presents with a violaceous plaque on the sole. Biopsy shows proliferating spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated erythrocytes. The causative virus is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8 / KSHV). In AIDS-associated KS, it occurs at low CD4 counts. Histology shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, hyaline globules, and plasma cells. Treatment for AIDS-KS includes antiretroviral therapy and liposomal doxorubicin.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman presents with painful genital ulcers that are soft and tender, with undermined edges. The inguinal lymph nodes are tender and fluctuant (bubo). Gram stain shows 'school of fish' pattern. Causative organism is:
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. It presents with a soft, painful ulcer with undermined edges and tender inguinal bubo (painful lymphadenopathy). Gram stain shows bipolar-staining Gram-negative rods in 'school of fish' or 'railway track' pattern. Treatment: azithromycin 1 g single dose or ceftriaxone 250 mg IM.

questions.q: A patient with leprosy develops sudden onset painful swelling of a leprous plaque with fever and raised ESR. Slit-skin smear shows BI of 4+. This reaction is best classified as:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL / Type 2 reaction) occurs in BL and LL leprosy (high BI), presenting with tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic features. It is immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity). Type 1 (reversal) reaction occurs in borderline leprosy and is a Type IV (DTH) reaction.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, telangiectasia, and calcinosis. Anti-centromere antibodies are positive. The most feared complication specific to this subset is:
questions.exp: Limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc / CREST syndrome) is associated with anti-centromere antibodies. Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) — not pulmonary fibrosis — is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in lcSSc. Scleroderma renal crisis (hypertensive emergency) is associated with diffuse SSc and anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies.

questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with hypopigmented scaly macules over the upper back and chest that coalesce into large patches. KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. Wood's lamp reveals golden-yellow fluorescence. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor (Malassezia furfur/globosa) shows characteristic short curved hyphae and yeast cells ('spaghetti and meatballs') on KOH mount. Wood's lamp reveals golden-yellow to yellow-green fluorescence. Vitiligo shows chalk-white fluorescence; it is depigmented, not scaly. Treatment: selenium sulfide, ketoconazole shampoo, or oral fluconazole.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-coloured crusted plaques around the mouth and nose. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. The most common causative organism in India is:
opts: Mixed S. aureus and S. pyogenes
questions.exp: Impetigo (non-bullous) is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus in most settings today (previously Streptococcus pyogenes was primary). In India, S. aureus is the predominant organism. Treatment: topical mupirocin or fusidic acid for localised disease; oral cloxacillin/cefalexin for widespread disease.

questions.q: A dermatologist plans to perform a punch biopsy of a 6 mm lesion on the back. Which anaesthetic is MOST appropriate for local infiltration?
questions.exp: Lignocaine 1% with 1:100,000 adrenaline (epinephrine) is the standard for most dermatological procedures. Adrenaline causes vasoconstriction, reducing bleeding and prolonging anaesthesia. Maximum safe dose of lignocaine with adrenaline is 7 mg/kg; without adrenaline is 3-4 mg/kg. Adrenaline is safe on the trunk/back.

questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with multiple flesh-coloured papules on the shaft of penis. Acetowhitening is positive. PCR confirms HPV type 6. The patient asks about recurrence. The vaccine that would have been most protective is:
questions.exp: Condylomata acuminata (genital warts) are caused by HPV types 6 and 11 (low-risk types). Both the quadrivalent (Gardasil) and nonavalent (Gardasil 9) vaccines cover HPV 6 and 11. The bivalent vaccine (Cervarix) covers only HPV 16 and 18. Therefore, both quadrivalent and nonavalent vaccines provide protection against genital warts.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules, V-sign, and shawl sign with proximal muscle weakness. CK is markedly elevated. Anti-Mi-2 antibody is positive. This antibody is associated with:
questions.exp: Anti-Mi-2 antibodies (anti-nuclear helicase/ATPase) are found in ~20% of DM and are associated with classic dermatomyositis with good prognosis and good response to treatment. Anti-MDA5 is associated with amyopathic DM and ILD. Anti-TIF1γ (p155/140) is associated with malignancy-associated DM. Anti-Jo-1 is associated with antisynthetase syndrome with ILD.

questions.q: A 42-year-old man presents with painless ulceration of the nasal septum with beefy-red granulation tissue and 'kissing lesions'. Biopsy shows Donovan bodies (Calymmatobacterium granulomatis / Klebsiella granulomatis). Drug of choice is:
opts: Doxycycline 100 mg BD for minimum 3 weeks
questions.exp: Donovanosis (Granuloma inguinale) caused by Klebsiella granulomatis shows intracytoplasmic Donovan bodies within mononuclear cells on biopsy. DOC is doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for at least 3 weeks (until complete healing). Azithromycin 1 g weekly is an alternative. Kissing lesions are characteristic.

questions.q: A 30-year-old presents with diffuse hair loss after delivering a baby 3 months ago. Trichogram shows >25% telogen hairs. The most likely diagnosis and expected course is:
opts: Telogen effluvium — spontaneous recovery in 6-12 months
Anagen effluvium — complete recovery after stopping causative agent
questions.exp: Postpartum telogen effluvium occurs 2-5 months post-delivery due to shift of hairs from anagen to telogen triggered by the hormonal changes. It is self-limiting, with spontaneous recovery typically within 6-12 months. Trichogram showing >15-25% telogen hairs confirms telogen effluvium. No specific treatment required; reassurance is key.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a non-healing ulcer on the lower lip for 6 months with indurated edges. He is a chronic smoker. Biopsy shows well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with keratin pearls. Sentinel lymph node biopsy is indicated when tumour thickness exceeds:
questions.exp: For cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is generally considered for tumours >4 mm thickness (per NCCN guidelines) or tumours with Clark level ≥IV and other high-risk features. SCC of the lip is a high-risk variant. For melanoma, SLNB threshold is >1 mm (or 0.75-1 mm with adverse features).

questions.q: A 10-year-old presents with annular erythematous plaques with central clearing and advancing scaly border on the trunk. KOH mount shows branching septate hyphae. The most likely causative dermatophyte in India is:
questions.exp: Trichophyton rubrum is the most common dermatophyte causing tinea corporis globally and in India. However, in recent years there has been a dramatic rise of T. indotineae (formerly classed under T. mentagrophytes) in India, causing recalcitrant/widespread tinea due to terbinafine resistance. T. rubrum remains the most prevalent overall. Microsporum canis is common in tinea capitis from animal contact.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with palpable purpura on bilateral lower limbs, arthralgia, haematuria, and abdominal pain. Biopsy shows leucocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposits on DIF. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura) classically presents with the tetrad of palpable purpura (legs/buttocks), arthralgia, abdominal pain, and renal involvement. DIF shows IgA deposits in small vessel walls — pathognomonic. It is a small vessel vasculitis (IgA-mediated immune complex). ANCA is associated with MPA and GPA.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the lip, recurring every 2 months triggered by sunlight. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. He requests suppressive antiviral therapy. The recommended regimen is:
opts: Acyclovir 200 mg 5 times daily for 5 days
questions.exp: Recurrent herpes labialis (HSV-1) with frequent recurrences (≥6/year) or significant impact benefits from daily suppressive therapy. Valacyclovir 500 mg OD (or 1 g OD) is the preferred suppressive regimen due to once-daily dosing and better bioavailability than acyclovir. Acyclovir 400 mg BD is an alternative. Episodic therapy (5-day courses) is for infrequent episodes.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with pruritic erythematous papules and vesicles on the flexural surfaces of elbows and behind knees since childhood. She has elevated total IgE and personal history of asthma. Skin biopsy shows spongiosis. Mutation in which gene is most commonly associated with atopic dermatitis?
questions.exp: Loss-of-function mutations in Filaggrin (FLG) are the strongest known genetic risk factor for atopic dermatitis, found in ~30-50% of European patients. Filaggrin is essential for the epidermal barrier; its deficiency leads to trans-epidermal water loss and sensitisation. SPINK5 mutations cause Netherton syndrome.

questions.q: A patient with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis uncontrolled with topical corticosteroids and tacrolimus is started on dupilumab. What is the mechanism of action?
opts: Anti-IL-4Rα blocking IL-4 and IL-13 signalling
questions.exp: Dupilumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-4Rα (IL-4 receptor alpha subunit), blocking signalling of both IL-4 and IL-13 — key drivers of Th2 inflammation in AD. It is the first approved biologic for moderate-to-severe AD. Nemolizumab targets IL-31 receptor. Omalizumab is anti-IgE. Baricitinib/upadacitinib are JAK inhibitors.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with multiple comedones, papules, pustules, and a few nodules on face and back. He has been on benzoyl peroxide for 2 months with partial response. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Add topical retinoid (adapalene) plus oral doxycycline
Switch to topical azelaic acid alone
questions.exp: For moderate acne (papules, pustules, few nodules) inadequately controlled with benzoyl peroxide, adding a topical retinoid (adapalene) plus an oral antibiotic (doxycycline 100 mg OD/BD) is the recommended next step per international guidelines (NICE, AAD). Oral isotretinoin is reserved for severe nodulo-cystic acne or acne unresponsive to two courses of antibiotic therapy.
